items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: I’m always going to love them — B.B. King — like a father to me. The point is is that they called me to do a

ctx.x: Exactly. You want Steve, you call him. I’ll be glad to call him for you. But you know when I was coming along I didn’t know that that’s the way it was. You had to play like somebody else in order to do that. Well I didn’t. I played me. But I played and did the job. Now I was fortunate enough to have enough in me to do the job plus. That’s what I’ve done all my life. Do the job plus stick a little bit of me in. And that’s how I’ve done over all these years. I’m going to go in and I’m going to do the job. I’m going…

job and I said yes I can do it. That’s what I’m going to do. But I get along with everybody and no matter who it is. Cissy, Whitney, it doesn’t matter. That to me is part of life. That’s why I’m in the position that I’m in, that’s why I like everybody, that’s why I can talk about everybody. But I always have something positive to say. Now I could go and I could have made a million dollars instead if I’d have talked about all the bad things about Aretha while I was there. For what? Then I’d never work.
